formulas.formula: Plan the year, track every dollar, and know your profit.
1. Budget Plan: type the year, your starting cash, and what you expect to bring in each month from each revenue stream.
2. Still on Budget Plan: list your expenses with a group and a monthly amount. Busy season or a big one-off? Type over that month's cell.
3. Transactions: log every sale deposit and every business expense with its category.
4. Budget vs Actual: pick a month to see each line against its budget, plus the year so far.
5. Profit & Loss, Cash Flow, Year Summary and Dashboard update on their own.
Revenue is what comes in. Profit is what's left after every expense.
What you spend to make or deliver what you sell (materials, packaging, shipping). Revenue minus this is your gross profit.
Uses your real numbers for months with activity, and your budget for the months still ahead, so you can see if cash gets tight.
Log a refund as a minus amount on the same category.
On Transactions, select columns B to G from row 6 down and press Delete.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Green: ahead of budget (more revenue, or less spending).
Yellow: a month you typed over on Budget Plan, or worth a look.
Red: behind budget, a loss, or a category that isn't on Budget Plan.
Thank you for your purchase! Here's to a profitable year.

Pick a month. Left columns: that month. Right columns: the year so far (January through that month).
Your real results by month: revenue, cost of goods, gross profit, operating expenses by group, and net profit.

formulas.formula: Real money in and out for months with activity. Months with no activity yet use your budget, so the Projected column shows where cash is heading.
Plan a normal month in Monthly Amount: it fills January to December. Type over any month that's different.

Every deposit and every business expense, one row each. Pick the category from Budget Plan.
Every line, every month: what really came in and went out, against the budget for the year.
